description: Figure 2 is a conceptual diagram illustrating a hierarchical taxonomy for medical ethics. It is structured as a concentric circular chart, with an inner circle and an outer circle. The inner circle represents the four foundational pillar principles of medicine, while the outer circle, which surrounds the inner one, is divided into 26 distinct segments, each corresponding to a category. These 26 categories are described as being clustered from a total of 256 more detailed ethical principles. The figure visually conveys the relationship between the broad, high-level principles and the more granular, specific categories that fall under them, forming a structured framework for evaluating medical ethics. The diagram is presented in grayscale, with no color coding or numerical data labels visible within the circles themselves.
